name: Kepler-452b
tagline: Il cugino della Terra — il primo mondo delle dimensioni della Terra in una zona abitabile di gemello solare.

facts.label: Stella madre
facts.value: Kepler-452 — a G2 Sun twin ~6 billion years old

history: Kepler-452b made the front pages in 2015: a world just 60% larger than Earth orbiting a star almost indistinguishable from the Sun, at a distance where a year is 385 days and the received starlight is nearly Earth's. It sits in the habitable zone of a star 1.5 billion years older than ours — an ancient, brighter cousin — so any surface has spent its life being gently boiled by a slowly warming sun. Whether it is rocky or a gaseous mini-Neptune remains unresolved; its mass is inferred, not measured. Either way it re-wrote the odds on how common Earth-like worlds might be.
source: Kepler transit survey — Jenkins et al. (2015)
